title: Scotch Eggs
subtitle: Soft-boiled eggs wrapped in sausagemeat and deep-fried
excerpt: Soft-boiled eggs encased in seasoned sausagemeat, coated in breadcrumbs, and deep-fried until golden. The yolk should be soft and jammy, the meat cooked through, the crust shatteringly crisp.

recipe.sourceNotes: Scotch eggs are a British picnic and pub food classic, first commercially made by Fortnum and Mason in London in 1738, though the concept of encasing a boiled egg in meat is much older. The classic Scotch egg uses a hard-boiled egg, but the modern revival of the dish (driven partly by the London gastropub movement of the 2000s and 2010s) favours a soft, jammy centre. The sausagemeat is typically seasoned with mustard and herbs to complement the egg. The three-stage coating — flour, egg, breadcrumbs — provides the crisp outer crust that distinguishes a properly made Scotch egg from a pale, soft version. Scotch eggs are associated with British picnics, buffets, and pub food but can equally be served warm as a starter with a dressed salad.

recipeTools.notes: A deep, heavy saucepan for deep frying. A thermometer for the oil temperature.

content.text: For a soft, jammy yolk, boil the eggs for exactly 6 minutes and immediately transfer to iced water. Peel carefully under cold running water. The sausagemeat must be pressed into a thin, even layer around the egg with no gaps or thin spots or the coating will crack during frying. Fry at 170 C: lower and the meat will be greasy; higher and the crust will burn before the meat is cooked. A meat thermometer inserted into the centre should read 75 C when done.

content.text: Boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes. Transfer to iced water immediately. Peel carefully. Mix the sausagemeat with the mustard, thyme leaves, salt, and pepper.

Divide the sausagemeat into 4 portions. Flatten each into a thin round. Roll the peeled eggs in flour and place one in the centre of each sausagemeat round. Wrap the sausagemeat around the egg, pressing to seal with no gaps. Roll each in flour, dip in the beaten egg, then roll in the breadcrumbs to coat thoroughly.

Heat the oil in a deep, heavy saucepan to 170 C. Fry 2 Scotch eggs at a time for 7 to 8 minutes, turning occasionally, until deeply golden. Drain on kitchen paper. Serve warm or at room temperature, cut in half to reveal the jammy yolk.
